subject: Critical Thinking
title: Propositional Logic: The Language of Reasoning
description: A quick, practical guide to Propositional Logic: The Language of Reasoning.

hook.text: What if you could write any argument as a formula and check it like math? That's propositional logic.

buildup.text: It uses symbols: P, Q for statements. ∧ for AND, ∨ for OR, ¬ for NOT, → for IF-THEN.

discovery.text: 'If it rains AND I have no umbrella, THEN I get wet' becomes: (R ∧ ¬U) → W. Clean and testable.

twist.text: George Boole invented this in 1854. Nobody cared — until it became the foundation of all computing.

climax.text: Every digital circuit, search engine, and database query runs on propositional logic.

punchline.text: A Victorian math hobby powers the modern world.

quiz.question: Who invented the symbolic logic that underpins modern computing?

details.summary: Propositional logic uses symbols and connectives (and, or, not, if-then) to represent the logical structure of statements. It strips away content to reveal pure form, allowing mechanical evaluation of argument validity.
details.whyItMatters: Propositional logic is the foundation of computer science, mathematics, and any domain that requires rigorous formal reasoning.
takeaways: Propositions are statements that are either true or false
Logical connectives combine propositions into complex statements
Formal symbolism reveals structure hidden in natural language

faq.question: What are the basic connectives in propositional logic?
faq.answer: AND (conjunction), OR (disjunction), NOT (negation), IF-THEN (conditional), and IF AND ONLY IF (biconditional). Each has precise truth-functional definitions.

faq.question: Why translate natural language arguments into propositional logic?
faq.answer: Natural language is ambiguous. Symbolic notation removes ambiguity, making it possible to check validity mechanically using truth tables or proof rules.
